subject: Post-call: Maple Health — SLOs, topology constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Maple Health — SLOs, topology constraints & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the 30-minute call this morning. Quick recap below so we have alignment and clear next steps for the technical deep-dive with your engineering team. I included Jasmine (solutions engineering) and Marissa (customer success) who will be on the follow-up.

Summary of pain & goals
- Primary pain: inference latency causing a poor clinician experience in the triage UI (slow suggestions on diagnosis snippets).
- Goal: P95 generation latency at or under 200ms for 512-token inference in production for the triage path; sustained throughput target ~100–150 req/s per region during business hours with burst capacity to 300 req/s.
- Data residency: production data must remain in a customer VPC (no PII to leave the VPC).

Technical constraints called out on the call
- Primary topology: private deployment (VPC) behind your ingress; must integrate with your KMS for key management and use private peering to Redwood Private control-plane.
- Model: want to serve a fine-tuned open model. Initial plan is to test with redwood/longform-13b-8bit; fallback path to redwood/longform-7b-8bit for cost-sensitive flows.
- Observability & compliance: need token-level audit logs and request traces for SOC 2 evidence (retain 90 days by default).

Immediate next steps (owners & dates)
1) Share SLO template and network diagram (attached) — Rafael — today (11 Jun).
2) Technical deep-dive with EngOps + infra (30–45 minutes) — Proposed: Wed 18 Jun 09:00 PT — Jasmine to lead demo of deployment options and kernel/quantization tradeoffs.
3) Provide example payloads and traffic profile (Maple) — Mark Thompson / engops@maplehealth.com — by Mon 16 Jun.
4) Draft mutual action plan and preliminary cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private (Redwood) — Marissa — by Thu 19 Jun.

Attachments: MAPLE_SLO_TEMPLATE.xlsx (SLO table + token budget), maple-network-diagram.png (sketch of proposed networking/peering).

Open questions we want answered on the deep-dive
- Typical sequence lengths for triage (median / 95th percentile).
- Percent of requests that require streaming vs single-shot responses.
- Acceptable fallback behavior if control-plane capacity constrained (model variant fallback or degraded feature).

If that all looks right, please confirm the deep-dive slot on 2025-06-18 09:00 PT or suggest an alternate. Thanks!

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Maple Health — SLOs, topology constraints & next steps

Rafael — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side:

- Sequence lengths: median ~120 tokens, p95 ~520 tokens for the triage endpoint.
- Traffic profile: during clinic hours (08:00–18:00 PT) average 110 req/s across our three US clusters; spikes up to 260 req/s for short windows when batch job hits.
- Streaming: ~15% of requests are candidate-streaming type (partial results as tokens arrive).
- Security: we require HSM-backed KMS and circuit-level peering (no public internet).

We can get the sample payloads and a small anonymized dataset to Jasmine by Monday 16 Jun. Wed 18 Jun 09:00 PT works for the deep-dive — Mark and one EngOps engineer will join.

One more ask: can Redwood include an example fallback policy in the mutual action plan (e.g., route to smaller model with degraded response that includes a confidence flag)? That will help our product team approve the rollout window.

-Mark
Mark Thompson
Head of Infrastructure, Maple Health Systems
mark.thompson@maplehealth.com

On Wed, 11 Jun 2025 at 09:12 AM Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Maple Health — SLOs, topology constraints & next steps

Thanks Mark — great detail and exactly what we need for the deep-dive. Couple of clarifications and commitments from our side before Wednesday:

1) Fallback policy example: yes — we will include a recommended fallback policy in the MAP (mutual action plan). Proposal: primary route -> redwood/longform-13b-8bit (p95 target 200ms); fallback route -> redwood/longform-7b-8bit with explicit response metadata {"confidence_level","model_variant"} and a flag to surface degraded suggestions to the UI. Jasmine will show how that looks in the console during demo.
2) Streaming support: Redwood will show a streaming example and explain how streaming impacts p95 calculations and batching. For planning, assume streaming requests have slightly higher tail latency; we'll quantify on the call.
3) Deployment topology: we will prepare two concrete deployment blueprints for Wed —
   - Private (preferred): Redwood Private deployed to your VPC with private peering, KMS integration, and dedicated GPU pool (recommended for compliance and consistent latency).
   - Hybrid (fast path): Dedicated in Redwood-managed region with private peering + traffic routing rules to keep PII in your VPC where needed.
4) Cost & sizing: Marissa will produce a back-of-envelope cost for Dedicated vs Private and include burst provisioning options.

Action items restated
- Mark / engops: sample payloads + traffic profile by Mon 16 Jun.
- Rafael / Jasmine: SLO template + two deployment blueprints before Wed 18 Jun deep-dive.
- Marissa: initial cost sketch by Thu 19 Jun.

If anything above is incorrect or you want a different slot, say so — otherwise we’ll consider Wed 18 Jun 09:00 PT confirmed. Looking forward to the deep-dive.

— Rafael
